question: get_flow
answer:
1. `httpx.get(url, ...)` is re-exported from `_api.py`. It calls the module-level `request("GET", url, ...)`. [httpx/__init__.py](<work>/httpx-base/httpx/__init__.py:2) · [httpx/_api.py](<work>/httpx-base/httpx/_api.py:174)
2. `request()` creates a temporary synchronous `Client`, enters its context manager, and calls `Client.request(...)`. [httpx/_api.py](<work>/httpx-base/httpx/_api.py:101)
3. `Client.request()` calls `BaseClient.build_request()`, which merges client defaults and constructs a `Request`. Then `Client.request()` passes it to `Client.send()`. [httpx/_client.py](<work>/httpx-base/httpx/_client.py:771) · [httpx/_client.py](<work>/httpx-base/httpx/_client.py:340) · [httpx/_models.py](<work>/httpx-base/httpx/_models.py:382)
4. `Client.send()` resolves timeout, auth, and redirect settings, then calls `_send_handling_auth()` → `_send_handling_redirects()` → `_send_single_request()`. [httpx/_client.py](<work>/httpx-base/httpx/_client.py:879)
5. `_send_single_request()` uses `_transport_for_url()` to select the default or matching proxy transport, then hands off the request to `transport.handle_request(request)`. `HTTPTransport.handle_request()` converts it to an `httpcore.Request` and calls `self._pool.handle_request(req)`. [httpx/_client.py](<work>/httpx-base/httpx/_client.py:1001) · [httpx/_transports/default.py](<work>/httpx-base/httpx/_transports/default.py:230)
